Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 44, verses 10–16:

Explanation of the words:

Fa-ertaqib (فارتقب): i.e., wait.

Bi-dukhanin mubin (بدخان مبين): i.e., it is what a man of Quraysh would see from extreme hunger, a smoke between the sky and the earth.

Yaghshi al-nas (يغشى الناس): i.e., it veils their sight because of the severe exertion resulting from the intense hunger.

Rabbana ikshif 'annal-'adhab (ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب): i.e., O our Lord, if You remove the punishment from us, we will believe in You and in Your Messenger.

Anna lahumu al-dhikra (أنى لهم الذكرى): i.e., from what direction would remembrance come to them, when a clear Messenger has already come to them, yet they turned away from him and said, "a taught, possessed man" (mu'allamun majnun).

Mu'allamun majnun (معلم مجنون): i.e., he is taught the Qur'an by a human being; a majnun is one whose affairs are confused, not understanding what he says.

Innakum 'a'idun (إنكم عائدون): i.e., you will return to disbelief and denial.

Al-bathshat al-kubra (البطشة الكبرى): i.e., the strong seizure with which We seized them on the Day of Badr, when they were killed and taken captive.

The meaning of the verses:

The Exalted's saying, ﴿So wait﴾, the verse was revealed after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Quraysh on a day when their mockery of him and their derision of him and of the true religion he brought increased. He said, "O Allah, make it upon them as the years of Yusuf," that is, seven years of drought and famine. So his Lord commanded him to wait for that, and said to him, ﴿So wait for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful punishment.﴾ The Exalted responded to His Messenger, and afflicted Quraysh with drought and famine in which their livestock died and they suffered hunger, eating wool and drinking blood. A man would raise his head to the sky and see nothing but smoke veiling his sight from the severity of hunger, until they humbled themselves before Allah and sent to the Messenger asking him to invoke Allah, the Exalted, to lift this punishment from them. This is the meaning of the Exalted's saying: ﴿So wait for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful punishment. Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers.﴾ That is, in Your Messenger and in what he brought of guidance and the true religion.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿How will they have the reminder, when there had come to them a clear Messenger? Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught, possessed man."﴾ That is: and from where would remembrance come to them, so that they would turn back to their Lord and submit to Him, when a Messenger clarifying the truth has come to them, making it manifest to them? Therefore their remembrance and repentance were highly improbable. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed, you will return [to disbelief].﴾ And indeed Allah removed from them the punishment of famine, rain fell upon their lands, and their country prospered after a hardship that had lasted seven years; and they returned to polytheism and war against Islam and the Muslims.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿On the Day We will seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution.﴾ That is: and wait, O Our Messenger, for ﴿the Day We will seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution﴾. This occurred at Badr, where Allah took retribution upon them, killing their men, indeed their chieftains, and taking captive whoever among them was captured, and it was a seizure the likes of which Quraysh had never known.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The truth of Allah's promise to His Messenger and the answering of his supplication ﷺ (ﷺ).

2- Faith at the sight of punishment is neither beneficial nor useful.

3- A statement of how Quraysh met the call of Islam with denial and ingratitude.

4- The Qur'an's report of the unseen, and its truthfulness in that, is a sign that it is the revelation and speech of Allah, the Exalted.

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa niʿmatin kānū fīhā fākihīn﴾ (And blessings in which they had been rejoicing): i.e., the freshness and sweetness of life, in which they had been living in luxury.

﴿Fa-mā bakat ʿalayhimu l-samāʾu wa l-arḍ﴾ (So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them): i.e., because of their humiliation before God on account of their disbelief and wrongdoing.

﴿Wa mā kānū munẓarīn﴾ (Nor were they reprieved): i.e., given respite so that they might repent.

﴿Min al-ʿadhābi l-muhīn﴾ (From the humiliating punishment): i.e., the killing of their sons and the enslavement of their women.

﴿Wa la-qad ikhtarnāhum ʿalā ʿilmin ʿalā l-ʿālamīn﴾ (And We certainly chose them, with knowledge, over the worlds): i.e., We chose them with Our knowledge over the peoples of their time, from humankind and jinn. This was because of the many prophets among them and from them.

﴿Wa ātaynāhum mina l-āyāti mā fīhi balāʾun mubīn﴾ (And We gave them of the signs that which contained a manifest trial): i.e., We gave them blessings that contained a manifest trial, clear like the splitting of the sea, the manna and the quail.

Meaning of the verses

The noble context continues with the story of Moses, peace be upon him, and the enemy of God, Pharaoh, may the curses of the Most Merciful be upon him. God the Exalted says: ﴿Kam tarakū min jannāt﴾, i.e., how much Pharaoh and his soldiers, who perished with him in the sea, left behind: they left many gardens, i.e., orchards and flowing springs by which crops were irrigated, ﴿wa maqāmin karīm﴾, i.e., good dwellings and adorned gatherings decorated with all kinds of adornment (al-maḥfil being the place of gathering), ﴿wa niʿmatin kānū fīhā fākihīn﴾, i.e., great enjoyment in which they were rejoicing, i.e., living in ease and luxury. His saying, the Exalted: "Thus it was; so We made them inherit these," i.e., their blessing was thus: We took it away from them because of their disbelief in Us and their arrogance toward Our laws and Our friends. ﴿Wa awrathnāhā qawman ākharīn﴾ are the Children of Israel, when they returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fa-mā bakat ʿalayhimu l-samāʾu wa l-arḍ﴾, because they were disbelievers who had done no good on earth, and no good deed of theirs had ascended to heaven. So why should they be wept for? Rather, the believer is wept for by the earth on which he prostrated and worshipped God, and by the heaven to which his righteous deed ascended every day and night. His saying: ﴿wa mā kānū munẓarīn﴾, i.e., they were not given respite; rather the Lord hastened the punishment upon them, and did not give them respite so that they might repent, because of God's knowledge of the sealing of their hearts, and how they had promised Moses that if the punishment were lifted from them they would believe, yet they did not believe. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Wa la-qad najjaynā banī Isrāʾīl min al-ʿadhābi l-muhīn﴾, these are some of His favours upon the Children of Israel: that He saved them from the humiliating punishment which Pharaoh and his people inflicted upon them, when they slaughtered their sons and kept their women alive for service and degradation. What humiliating punishment is greater than this? ﴿Min Firʿawn﴾, i.e., from the punishment of Pharaoh which he would inflict upon them; ﴿innahu kāna ʿāliyan mina l-musrifīn﴾, i.e., Pharaoh was a tyrant and a transgressor, one of those who were extravagant in disbelief and wrongdoing. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Wa la-qad ikhtarnāhum﴾, i.e., the Children of Israel, ʿalā ʿilm, i.e., with Our knowledge, ʿalā l-ʿālamīn, i.e., over the worlds of their time, from the two weighty ones, humankind and jinn. His saying: ﴿Wa ātaynāhum﴾, i.e., We gave them of the signs ﴿mā fīhi balāʾun mubīn﴾, i.e., a great test. Among those signs were the splitting of the sea, the cloud shading them, and the manna and quail in the wilderness, and other things which were a great trial for them: would they give thanks or would they disbelieve?

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of God's way of removing blessings and sending retribution upon those who disbelieve God's blessings and do not thank Him, who disobey their Lord and obey their desires and their selves, who abandon prayer, follow lusts, abandon the Qur'an, occupy themselves with songs, turn away from the remembrance of God, and turn toward the remembrance of this world and its allurements.

2- Explanation of the humiliation of the people of disbelief and corruption before God and before the whole of creation, and the honour of the people of faith and piety before God and before the whole of creation, to the extent that heaven and earth weep for them when they die.

3- Condemnation of haughtiness on earth, which is arrogance and extravagance in everything.

4- Explanation that God tests His servants, i.e., examines them, with good and with evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 44, verse 34–42:

Explanation of the words:

Inna hā'ulā' (إنّ هؤلاء): i.e., the polytheists from Quraysh.

In hiya illā mawtatunā al-ūlā (إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى): i.e., there is no life after it and no death; this is a denial of the Final Resurrection.

Wa mā naḥnu bi-munshirīn (وما نحن بمنشرين): i.e., we will not be resurrected alive from our graves after our death.

Fa'tū bi-ābā'inā in kuntum ṣādiqīn (فأتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين): i.e., so bring forth, O Muhammad, our fathers who have died, if you are truthful in claiming that we will be resurrected alive from our graves after we die.

Ahum khayrun am qawmu Tubba' wa-alladhīna min qablihim (أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم): i.e., are these polytheists better in strength and power, or the people of Tubba' and those before them, such as 'Ād?

Ahlaknāhum innahum kānū mujrimīn (أهلكناهم إنهم كانوا مجرمين): i.e., We sent down Our punishment upon them and destroyed them, for they were a criminal people.

Lā'ibīn (لاعبين): i.e., playing in creating them, without a righteous purpose.

Mā khalaqnāhumā illā bil-ḥaqq (ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق): i.e., only for a matter that required their creation, namely that I be remembered and thanked in them.

Inna yawma al-faṣli mīqātuhum ajma'īn (إنّ يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين): i.e., indeed the Day of Judgment, on which creation is separated and their appointed time is decided, all of them, when Allah gathers them therein.

Yawma lā yughnī mawlan 'an mawlan shay'an (يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئاً): i.e., a day on which a relative cannot suffice his relative by averting any of the punishment from him.

Wa lā hum yunṣarūn (ولاهم ينصرون): i.e., none of them will help another.

Illā man raḥimahu Allāh (إلا من رحم الله): i.e., but whomever Allah has mercy upon, He will avert the punishment from him and grant him victory.

Innahu huwa al-'azīz al-raḥīm (إنه هو العزيز الرحيم): i.e., the Mighty, who prevails and takes vengeance upon His enemies, the Merciful toward His allies.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to seek the guidance of the people of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The stories of Moses and Pharaoh were mentioned only as a warning and reminder, so that they might take heed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, these⦆ — the lowest, whose minds have descended to the worst levels — are without shame or modesty, and they say ﴿It is only our first death﴾, denying resurrection and recompense, so that they may persist in their disbelief and immorality. Therefore they said ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾, i.e., raised alive from our graves as you promise us, O Muhammad. And if you insist on your claim of a second life, then ﴿bring our fathers who have died, if you are truthful﴾ in that. Their saying "bring" and "if you are truthful" is not out of honoring the Messenger ﷺ, but out of a feeling on their part that he is not alone in this call, but that behind him is one who backs him in it.

As for His saying, ﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them, for they were criminals﴾: they are not better than them in any way, neither in wealth nor in men. Just as We destroyed them, We will destroy these, and We destroyed the earlier ones because they were criminals, i.e., against themselves through polytheism and sins. These too are criminals, so they deserve destruction and will be destroyed if they do not repent, believe, affirm the Oneness of Allah, and obey Allah and His Messenger.

As for His saying, ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾, We created them only with truth, ﴿but most of them do not know﴾. This is evidence of resurrection and recompense, for it is not wise that Allah should create the universe for no purpose and then annihilate it with nothing beyond that. This would be the play and vanity from which intelligent people are far removed, so how much more so the Giver of intellects, may He be glorified and exalted. He created the universe only so that He would be remembered and thanked therein. Whoever remembers Him and thanks Him, He honors and rewards with the best reward; whoever abandons Him and disbelieves, He humiliates and rewards with the worst reward. This is accomplished after the end of this life and the existence of the second life, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is their appointed time, all of them﴾, i.e., indeed the Day of Resurrection is the day of the decisive judgment among people concerning what they differed over regarding monotheism and polytheism, righteousness and immorality, and it is their appointed time when all of them will be present: ﴿a day on which no relative will avail another relative anything, nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., a day on which no one, even a close relative such as a cousin, can suffice another by averting any of the punishment from him, nor will they help one another as they did in the world. And His saying, ﴿except for whom Allah has mercy﴾, i.e., but whoever Allah has mercy upon in this world through faith and monotheism, He will have mercy upon in the Hereafter, and a friend of His friends will intercede for him. Indeed He, the Exalted, is the Mighty, i.e., the One who takes vengeance on His enemies, the Merciful toward His allies. People are divided between a friend of Allah and an enemy: His friends are the believers, and His enemies are the disbelievers and the wicked.

Lessons of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense.

2- Criminality is the cause of destruction and ruin, whoever its doer may be.

3- Tubba' al-Himyari was a righteous servant and ruler; his people were disbelievers, so Allah destroyed them and saved him and the righteous believers with him. In this righteous king is a lesson for whoever takes heed.

4- The Lord, the Exalted, is exempt from play and vanity in what He creates and bestows, and in what He takes, gives and withholds.

5- The Day of Judgment, which is the Day of Decision, is the appointed time of all creation, when they are gathered for the separation of judgment.

6- Kinship, friendship and companionship will not benefit on the Day of Resurrection, but faith and righteous deeds will.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 44, verses 51–59:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing are in a secure place﴾: that is, those who feared their Lord in this world, believed, and did righteous deeds after abstaining from polytheism and sins, are in a secure assembly, where no fear will touch them at all.

﴿In gardens and springs﴾: this is the secure place.

﴿Of fine green silk and brocade﴾: that is, the finest silk and what is thick of it.

﴿Facing one another﴾: that is, none of them looks at the back of another, because the couches turn with them.

﴿Thus, and We will marry them﴾: that is, the matter is thus, and We will marry them.

﴿To wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn)﴾: that is, to women with white skin and wide eyes.

﴿Calling for every kind of fruit therein﴾: that is, they ask the attendants to bring them every kind of fruit.

﴿Secure﴾: that is, from its ending, from its harms, and from every fearful thing.

﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾: that is, but the first death, they have already tasted it.

﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾: that is, We made the Qur'an easy in your language.

﴿That they may remember﴾: that is, that they may take heed, so they believe and affirm the oneness of God, but they do not believe.

﴿So wait, for they are waiting﴾: that is, so wait for their destruction, for they are waiting for your destruction.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned the condition of the people of the Fire, He followed it by mentioning the condition of the people of Paradise, and this is the method of encouragement and warning that characterizes the Noble Qur'an, because it is a book of call and guidance in addition to being a book of legislation and rulings. So He, the Mighty, said: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing are in a secure place, in gardens and springs﴾. He, the Exalted, informed that those who feared Him in this world, believed in Him, obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions, and did not associate anything with Him, are in a secure place, that is, a safe assembly where no fear will reach them. He explained that secure place with His saying ﴿in gardens﴾, that is, orchards and springs. They wear, that is, their garments are of ﴿sundus﴾ and ﴿istabraq﴾; sundus is the finer silk and istabraq is what is thick of it. His saying "facing one another" means that none of them looks at the back of another, because the couches on which they sit turn around. ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing are in a secure place﴾: that is, those who feared their Lord in this world, believed, and did righteous deeds after abstaining from polytheism and sins, are in a secure assembly, where no fear will touch them at all.

﴿In gardens and springs﴾: this is the secure place.

﴿Of fine green silk and brocade﴾: that is, the finest silk and what is thick of it.

﴿Facing one another﴾: that is, none of them looks at the back of another, because the couches turn with them.

﴿Thus, and We will marry them﴾: that is, the matter is thus, and We will marry them.

﴿To wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn)﴾: that is, to women with white skin and wide eyes.

﴿Calling for every kind of fruit therein﴾: that is, they ask the attendants to bring them every kind of fruit.

﴿Secure﴾: that is, from its ending, from its harms, and from every fearful thing.

﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾: that is, but the first death, they have already tasted it.

﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾: that is, We made the Qur'an easy in your language.

﴿That they may remember﴾: that is, that they may take heed, so they believe and affirm the oneness of God, but they do not believe.

﴿So wait, for they are waiting﴾: that is, so wait for their destruction, for they are waiting for your destruction.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned the condition of the people of the Fire, He followed it by mentioning the condition of the people of Paradise, and this is the method of encouragement and warning that characterizes the Noble Qur'an, because it is a book of call and guidance in addition to being a book of legislation and rulings. So He, the Mighty, said: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing are in a secure place, in gardens and springs﴾. He, the Exalted, informed that those who feared Him in this world, believed in Him, obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions, and did not associate anything with Him, are in a secure place, that is, a safe assembly where no fear will reach them. He explained that secure place with His saying ﴿in gardens﴾, that is, orchards and springs. They wear, that is, their garments are of ﴿sundus﴾ and ﴿istabraq﴾; sundus is the finer silk and istabraq is what is thick of it. His saying "facing one another" means that none of them looks at the back of another, because the couches on which they sit turn around. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, the matter is thus, as We have described, and We will marry them to ḥūr ʿīn. The ḥūrāʾ are the white-skinned women, and one who has ḥawar in her eyes has a great whiteness of the eye over its blackness. ʿĪn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, meaning one with wide eyes. His saying ﴿calling therein for every kind of fruit, secure﴾: that is, they ask the attendants to bring them every kind of fruit, while they are secure from its ending, from its harm, and from every fearful thing that might befall them because of it or because of anything else.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾: that is, they will not taste death in Paradise after the first death which they tasted in this world, for its people do not fall ill, do not grow old, and do not die. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He protected them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾. This indicates that other than the God-fearing among the monotheists may taste the punishment of Hellfire before entering Paradise, unlike the God-fearing, who never enter the Fire at all. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A bounty from your Lord﴾: that is, that favor and honor was a bounty from your Lord, since they did not deserve it merely by their piety. The Messenger ﷺ said in the hadith of Muslim: "Be upright, come close to perfection, and rejoice, and know that none of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy and bounty." His saying: ﴿That is the great success﴾: that is, salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great success, as in His saying in Surat Āl ʿImrān: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded﴾ [Verse: 185].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue, that they may remember﴾: that is, We made the Qur'an easy in your Arabic language, that they may remember, take heed, believe, and be God-fearing. But most of them did not take heed. So wait, and watch what will befall them, for they are waiting for what will come to you of success or failure.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The virtue of piety and the honor of its people. Piety is fear of God that leads to obedience to God by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes.

2. A statement of some of the bliss of the people of Paradise, as encouragement to work for it.

3. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

4. Explanation of the wisdom behind making the Noble Qur'an easy to understand, which is taking heed, which necessitates piety.
